faq: What do you need to start?
Read access to a sample of your support replies, exported as a file or shared from your help desk. We choose a spread of topics and send you the list we plan to review.
Will you read private customer messages?
Only the replies in your sample, and we can work from copies with names and emails removed. We only use them for this review and delete them after delivery.
Does the review change anything in my system?
No. It is a report. Changes are listed so you or we can make them afterwards, and we can quote the fixes separately if you want us to do it.
Can you review replies written by humans?
Yes. The same checks apply, which is useful for training and for comparing staff replies with tool drafts. We keep feedback about people factual and kind.

desc:
A support reply quality review checks what your helper or drafting tool is really telling customers. Ecom Swift LLC reads a sample of your replies, scores them and writes up the problems with fixes, so you can correct mistakes before more customers see them.

## What is a support reply quality review?

A support reply quality review is a structured read of real customer replies, scored on accuracy, tone, policy match and clarity. Each problem is listed with the line that caused it and the likely reason. The output is a plain report with examples and exact fixes, such as a changed instruction or a missing help article.

## Why nobody should trust a reply tool unchecked

A helper can sound confident and still be wrong. It may quote an old return window, promise something you do not offer or answer in a tone that does not fit your brand. These errors rarely announce themselves. They show up later as a refund dispute, a bad review or a customer who simply stops buying.

Teams are usually too busy answering to audit their own tools. A review gives a fresh pair of eyes and a method, so problems are found by you first.

## How review improves accuracy and trust

Catching one wrong policy line can prevent the same mistake in many future replies, because a fix to the instruction or article changes every reply that follows. Review also shows patterns, such as a topic where the tool keeps guessing, which points to missing content instead of a one-off slip.

Tone matters as much as facts. Replies that sound cold, pushy or overly casual can hurt the relationship even when the information is right. The score for tone gives you a concrete way to see and adjust it.

## What a good review covers

- A fair sample of recent replies, taken across topics and channels.
- A score for accuracy against your real policies.
- A score for tone and match with your brand voice.
- A check of clarity, length and whether the customer question was answered.
- The likely cause of each problem, such as a wrong instruction or a gap in the content.
- The exact fix wording supplied, so you can paste it in.
- A list of help topics the tool lacked.
- A retest of fixed replies to confirm the problem is gone.
- Updated instructions ready to use.
- A simple routine for checking replies yourself each month.

## How we run it

You send us a sample of replies, exported or shared read-only, along with your policies and tone notes. We read each reply against those sources and score it. We then group the problems, trace each to its cause and write the fix. Nothing in your system is changed by the review itself. You decide which fixes to apply.

The Basic package reviews a small sample and lists the top problems. The Standard package reviews more replies, adds causes, exact fix wording and a retest. The Premium package covers a larger sample, supplies updated instructions, lists missing topics, gives you a monthly checking routine and ends with a results call.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Share replies from busy and quiet periods.
- Send the current version of your policies.
- Apply fixes one group at a time and retest.
- Keep the review report for future comparison.

**Avoid:**
- Sending only your best replies.
- Changing many instructions at once with no record.
- Treating a single poor reply as the whole picture.
- Leaving customer names in the sample when you can hide them.
- Skipping the retest after a fix.

## Who this is for

A store owner who installed a reply tool and has never read its output properly. A support manager who needs evidence before expanding automation. A team that has received a complaint about a wrong answer and wants to find the cause.

## What we need from you

A sample of recent replies, a copy of your policies and any tone notes you have. We work with read-only exports or shared access, never passwords, and we ask you to hide personal details where you can. Human-written replies can also be included if you want a comparison.
